sourceInformation.source: American football (over the top arcade style)
sourceInformation.genre: Arcade sports (7-on-7 American football) with beat-'em-up hit feel and a story campaign
sourceInformation.perspective: Sideline broadcast camera (a custom 50 degree view), Sky Cam and Blimp options, a Kick Cam behind the kicker for field goals, field-level, isometric and reverse replay angles
sourceInformation.tech: my-3D2dge v0.85.2 handoff (modified, see Engine Changes), AI Hub session client 1.4.0, the my-3D2dge mocap runtime with an 18-clip FIASCO set, Canvas 2D and Web Audio; Node 24.22.1 and Playwright 1.63.0 for tests
sourceInformation.artDirection: my-3D2dge native: HD Humanoid rigs drawn as pixel art at PS1 resolution, code-painted fields, stands and crowds, five lit stadiums with weather and particles; new football gear (helmets, pads, numbers), logos, play cards and Fiasco Card art
sourceInformation.animation: my-3D2dge procedural rigs and E.MOVES, joint post-processing (tilt, roll, lift) for dives, flights and pile-ups, and 18 motion-capture clips (Quaternius, Mesh2Motion, CMU) for throws, stances, blocks, falls, get-ups, dances and cheers
sourceInformation.audio: All in code: 11 original songs with layers and stings on the engine's chip synth, 50 synthesized sound effects, a crowd bed with reactions and chants, and a formant babble synth for Animalese and Simlish voices
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub Session Protocol v1, shared world, 1-4 players: the host runs the world and sends snapshots at 14 Hz; each client predicts its own player (the host accepts its reported position unless locked; measured within 2 yd of the host 98% of the time at 150 ms latency and 5% loss) from its own stick (snapped back past 2 yards), interpolates the rest, and runs its own play-call screen and kick meter; local 1-4 players on one machine
sourceInformation.testing: Allowed: headless tests with game.advance and game.debug, a scripted playthrough of the whole game, one command that prints only failures and a count, and screenshots only for what a script can't check. Used: npm test -- --browser (16 suites: rules, AI, story playthrough from the prologue to the credits, attract loop, 2-4 player netcode with latency and loss including a measured prediction error, TASK.md requirements, real-browser voice synthesis, and the AI Hub harness in all 4 configurations); test/bands.mjs, the plan's Play Lab bands at n = 30 (all 17 plays inside); Playwright screenshots including the 1920x1080 look check; and the engine's check tool
sourceInformation.research: none beyond the engine's and the AI Hub's own documentation
sourceInformation.environment: Claude Code CLI (headless); Linux; browser unknown
sourceInformation.usage: unknown: no token or cost figures are visible to me in this session; session time about 2 hours 20 minutes (07:06 to about 09:25 local, by the file timestamps)

testingFeedback: 43 game issues, each fixed and logged with its fix in ISSUES.md: 15 found by the headless suites (for example a new match replaying the previous match's play calls, a kick-play crash, the touch-only gate unlocking itself, five attract segments missing their key moment), 17 by browser runs and screenshots (for example an em dash drawn as '?' in the Hall of Fiasco at the 1080p look check, three crashes and a syntax error, a black field from a wrong color conversion, 12 fps from the field rebaking on every zoom change, '?' glyphs), and 9 by the Play Lab and the plan's bands (for example runs averaging 13 yards, a pass rush sacking in 0.8 s, blocks that never broke off). Two more after the log was first closed: the Hall of Fiasco skipped games whose local side was CPU-driven (a behavioural records test), and online prediction kept the player within 2 yards of the host only 72% of the time at 150 ms latency (a netcode measurement; now 98%). Test bugs and the machine's full /tmp are listed there separately and not counted.

9, listed in ISSUES.md: the boot crash, the input crash, the update crash, the syntax error that stopped the page loading, the black field, the stale play calls (they broke REMATCH, story retries and every scripted situation), the kick-play crash, 12 fps rendering, and the 0.8 s pass rush.

The rules suite's set-situation runs: replaying scenarios back to back exposed that a new match kept the previous match's play calls, a bug that silently broke REMATCH and chapter retries. The scripted story playthrough (prologue, nine drills by their bots, four matches, halftime choices, the ending, the credits, a loss and RETRY) was the best broad net.

My first spin-evasion test: as written it could never fail, so it proved nothing until I rewrote it to call the tackle directly inside and outside the spin's window. The engine check tool's cycling through iso, side and the other stock views also told me little, since the game uses its own broadcast view.
engineFeedback: The HD Humanoid with the motion-capture runtime (a throw, a three-point stance or a breakdance on any rig in one line), and the exact fixed-step headless game.advance, which made a 940-check test suite, a Play Lab and a whole-game scripted playthrough run in about a minute without a browser. The free pause, settings, controls and save screens saved a lot of work.

Yes: I assumed E.hex returned an integer (it returns [r, g, b]) and got a black field; I used input._used as my own flag and broke the engine's input; I didn't know each camera zoom value makes a new floor bake, so a smoothly zooming camera rebaked the whole field every frame; and I called game.go from a deep link before the browser boot steps finished.

The football simulation itself: rules, downs, the clock, kicks, possession and scoring; 14 athletes with intents, collisions, blocking engagements and sheds; the AI brains (pass and run blocking, routes, QB reads, man and zone coverage, rush lanes, pursuit angles, ball-carrier steering with evasive moves) and the CPU coach. Second, the shared-world netcode adapter for the AI Hub.

Performance and caching that the API doesn't show: the floor bake per view and zoom (with a cache of 6), and finding which internals the Shell and settings rely on. Also the very large API surface: the right helper usually existed, but finding it took grepping.

E1 the PlayStation glyphs (and · ✓ ▲ ▼ ◂) in both pixel fonts, so prompts never draw '?'; E2 PlayStation symbols by default with Xbox as the option, shown on the Settings screen; E3 a gear hook in the HD Humanoid's draw for pads, numbers and the carried ball; E4 a football helmet hat style; E5 a per-letter voice function for E.Dialog; E6 named audio buses; E7 Dev settings kept off the Settings screen and settings rows on any Shell screen (the live tuning sliders); E8 opening Settings without pausing (AI Hub sessions); E10 a floor-bake cache of 16 instead of 6. Each is logged in ENGINE-CHANGES.md.

Make TileMap floor bakes independent of zoom (bake at world resolution once and scale, or document loudly that every zoom level is a full rebake), and expose the pixel font's glyph bitmaps publicly so games can paint text into textures without reaching into E.font._glyph.
promptFeedback: It is concrete about the deliverables and how they will be checked (the file name, the exit interview's exact shape, the hub harness), and its 10-foot, controller-first UX rules are specific enough to act on: device-following prompts, PlayStation glyphs with an Xbox option, no dense web screens, the touch-only gate.

Two instructions pull against each other: TASK.md asks to pick the title with a real RNG while STAGE.md says to use the plan's title. And the plan's scope (6 teams, 5 stadiums, 5 story chapters, 9 drills, 16 attract segments, client-side prediction) is far more than one session at medium effort, so 'follow the plan' versus 'TASK.md wins' and 'no stubbed features' needed judgment about what to cut without leaving stubs.

Making 7-on-7 AI play believable football (blocking that neither collapses nor walls off every run, coverage, pursuit, QB reads) and keeping it balanced, together with shared-world multiplayer that passes the harness. The machine itself was a factor: /tmp was full, which crashed headless Chromium until I pointed TMPDIR at my own folder.

Give the expected scale (hours or a token budget) and let the plan mark must, should and could features, so cuts are deliberate. Say which of TASK.md and STAGE.md decides the title. Mention shared-machine limits such as a full /tmp.

aiHub.name: Hamerican Football
aiHub.description: Lead the hopeless Tumbleweed Junction Fiascos through the Fiasco Cup: 7-on-7 arcade football with turbo, Big Hits, Hot Streaks, trick plays and mascots, for 1-4 players.
aiHub.controls: Stick/WASD run · ✕/Space hike, dive, tackle · ✕○□ or 1-3/click throw · R2/Shift turbo · ○/L switch
